title: Ezekiel Chapter 7 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Ezekiel chapter 7 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Ezekiel Chapter 7 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Ezekiel Chapter 7.

questions.question: Who received the word of the LORD in Ezekiel 7?
options: The son of man
Moses
David
Isaiah
questions.correctAnswer: The son of man
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 7:1 states that the word of the LORD came unto Ezekiel, who is called 'the son of man.'

questions.question: To whom does the Lord GOD speak in Ezekiel 7:2?
options: The land of Israel
The people of Egypt
The city of Babylon
The tribes of Judah
questions.correctAnswer: The land of Israel
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 7:2 says the Lord GOD speaks to the land of Israel.

questions.question: What has come upon the land of Israel according to Ezekiel 7:3?
options: The end
Peace
Prosperity
Blessings
questions.correctAnswer: The end
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 7:3 states that the end has come upon Israel and that God will send His anger and judge them.

questions.question: What will God not have toward the people in Ezekiel 7:4?
options: Pity
Joy
Anger
Love
questions.correctAnswer: Pity
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 7:4 says, 'mine eye shall not spare thee, neither will I have pity.'

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 7:5 says an evil, an only evil, has come.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 7:5 explicitly states, 'An evil, an only evil, behold, is come.'

questions.question: What is watching for the people according to Ezekiel 7:6?
options: The end
Peace
The morning
The harvest
questions.correctAnswer: The end
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 7:6 says, 'An end is come, the end is come: it watcheth for thee.'

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 7:7, what is near to those dwelling in the land?
options: The day of trouble
The day of joy
The day of harvest
The day of rest
questions.correctAnswer: The day of trouble
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 7:7 states, 'the day of trouble is near' for those dwelling in the land.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 7:8 promises that God will shortly pour out His mercy upon the people.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 7:8 says God will pour out His fury and accomplish His anger, not mercy.

questions.question: What will the Lord judge the people according to, as stated in Ezekiel 7:9?
options: Their ways and abominations
Their wealth
Their friends
Their sacrifices
questions.correctAnswer: Their ways and abominations
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 7:9 says God will judge according to their ways and abominations.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 7:10, what has blossomed?
options: The rod
The tree
The vine
The flower
questions.correctAnswer: The rod
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 7:10 states, 'the rod hath blossomed.'

questions.question: What shall rise up into a rod of wickedness according to Ezekiel 7:11?
options: Violence
Peace
Justice
Mercy
questions.correctAnswer: Violence
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 7:11 says, 'Violence is risen up into a rod of wickedness.'

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 7:12 states that the buyer should rejoice because wrath is not upon the multitude.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 7:12 says let not the buyer rejoice for wrath is upon all the multitude.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 7:13, will the seller return to what was sold?
options: No, the seller shall not return
Yes, immediately
Only if they repent
Only after many days
questions.correctAnswer: No, the seller shall not return
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 7:13 says the seller shall not return to that which is sold.

questions.question: What is the sequence of events mentioned in Ezekiel 7:14?
options: The trumpet is blown, but no one goes to battle
The battle begins and the trumpet is blown
The people go to battle without a trumpet
The trumpet sounds and people rejoice
questions.correctAnswer: The trumpet is blown, but no one goes to battle
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 7:14 states, 'They have blown the trumpet... but none goeth to the battle.'

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 7:15 describes that those in the city will die by the sword.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 7:15 says those in the field will die with the sword, but those in the city will die by famine and pestilence.

medium.title: Ezekiel Chapter 7 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Ezekiel Chapter 7 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 7:10, what signifies that the day of judgment has come?
options: The rod hath blossomed and pride hath budded
The trumpet has been blown to call to battle
The sword is without and famine within
The silver and gold shall not deliver in the day of wrath
questions.correctAnswer: The rod hath blossomed and pride hath budded
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 7:10 states 'Behold the day, behold, it is come: the morning is gone forth; the rod hath blossomed, pride hath budded,' indicating the arrival of judgment marked by pride and wickedness.

questions.question: What is described as 'a rod of wickedness' in Ezekiel 7:11?
options: Violence
Pride
Silver and gold
The trumpet sound
questions.correctAnswer: Violence
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 7:11 says 'Violence is risen up into a rod of wickedness,' showing that violence embodies the wicked instrument of punishment.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 7:12, what attitude toward buying and selling is warned against because of the coming wrath?
options: Buyers should not rejoice and sellers should not mourn
Buyers should rejoice and sellers should mourn
Both buyers and sellers should rejoice
Both buyers and sellers should mourn
questions.correctAnswer: Buyers should not rejoice and sellers should not mourn
questions.explanation: The verse warns 'let not the buyer rejoice, nor the seller mourn: for wrath is upon all the multitude thereof,' indicating no place for rejoicing or mourning amid coming judgment.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 7:13 say about the seller's ability to return to what was sold?
options: The seller shall not return to what was sold, even if alive
The seller will return and reclaim what was sold
The seller can strengthen himself in iniquity
The seller will be protected by the vision
questions.correctAnswer: The seller shall not return to what was sold, even if alive
questions.explanation: Verse 13 states sellers cannot regain what they sold even if alive, highlighting the irrevocable nature of judgment and the vision touching all.

questions.question: What practical lesson about preparation is taught in Ezekiel 7:14 where the trumpet is blown?
options: Despite readiness signals, no one goes to battle due to God's wrath
The trumpet calls everyone to fight and defend themselves
The people rejoice in the trumpet's sound as a sign of victory
The trumpet is ignored and the people continue in sin
questions.correctAnswer: Despite readiness signals, no one goes to battle due to God's wrath
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 7:14 says 'They have blown the trumpet... but none goeth to the battle: for my wrath is upon all the multitude thereof,' teaching that human readiness is futile against divine judgment.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 7:15, what are the two forms of judgment affecting those inside the city and those in the field?
options: Sword outside for those in the field; famine and pestilence inside the city
Fire for those in the field; sword inside the city
Famine for those in the field; pestilence inside the city
Pestilence outside the city; sword inside the city
questions.correctAnswer: Sword outside for those in the field; famine and pestilence inside the city
questions.explanation: Verse 15 explains a dual judgment: 'the sword is without, and the pestilence and the famine within,' differentiating the fate of those in the field and city.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 7:16 teach about those who escape the coming judgment?
options: They will be on the mountains like doves of the valleys, mourning for their iniquity
They will rejoice and celebrate deliverance
They will rebuild the city with gladness
They will become leaders of the people
questions.correctAnswer: They will be on the mountains like doves of the valleys, mourning for their iniquity
questions.explanation: The verse says survivors will be like mourning doves on mountains, showing sorrow and repentance for their sins.

questions.question: What physical and emotional conditions are described in Ezekiel 7:17-18 as a result of the coming judgment?
options: Feeble hands, weak knees, sackcloth, horror, shame, and baldness
Strong hands, firm knees, garments of joy, and celebration
Feeble hands, weak knees, but joyful faces and hair growth
Strong hands, weak knees, shame, but confident faces
questions.correctAnswer: Feeble hands, weak knees, sackcloth, horror, shame, and baldness
questions.explanation: Verses 17-18 describe physical weakness and mourning attire symbolizing deep shame and horror before God’s judgment.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 7:19 teaches that silver and gold will save the people on the day of the LORD's wrath.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 7:19 explicitly states silver and gold shall not deliver nor satisfy souls in the day of wrath, showing wealth cannot save from divine judgment.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 7:20 explain the reason God has removed the beauty and majesty of their ornaments?
options: Because they made images of their abominations and detestable things in them
Because they were stolen by strangers
Because they were given as offerings to the temple
Because they were lost in battle
questions.correctAnswer: Because they made images of their abominations and detestable things in them
questions.explanation: Verse 20 states their ornaments were defiled by idols and abominations, so God set them far away as a judgment.

questions.question: What consequence does Ezekiel 7:21 describe for the land of Israel because of their abominations?
options: Their possessions will be given to strangers and the wicked who will pollute them
They will be blessed with peace and prosperity
Their enemies will be defeated and driven away
Their wealth will be multiplied tenfold
questions.correctAnswer: Their possessions will be given to strangers and the wicked who will pollute them
questions.explanation: Verse 21 explains God will hand over their treasures to foreigners and wicked people who will defile them as punishment.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 7:22 warn will happen to God's secret place and holy places?
options: Robbers will enter and defile them, and God will turn His face away
They will be protected and kept holy
They will be rebuilt and glorified
They will be hidden and kept secret
questions.correctAnswer: Robbers will enter and defile them, and God will turn His face away
questions.explanation: Verse 22 states God will turn away His face, allowing robbers to pollute and defile His sanctuary as judgment.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 7:23, what is the land full of, requiring a chain to be made?
options: Bloody crimes
Joy and peace
Righteousness and faith
Harvest and plenty
questions.correctAnswer: Bloody crimes
questions.explanation: Verse 23 says the land is full of bloody crimes and the city full of violence, symbolizing the need for restraint and judgment.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 7:24 says God will bring the best of the heathen to possess the houses of Israel.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 7:24 says God will bring the worst of the heathen to possess their houses, emphasizing the severity of judgment.

questions.question: What is the significance of the consecutive mischief and rumours mentioned in Ezekiel 7:26 for the people seeking prophetic guidance?
options: The law will perish from priests and counsel from elders, leaving no true guidance
Prophets will multiply and guide the people faithfully
The people will find peace and understanding
The priests will renew the law and restore counsel
questions.correctAnswer: The law will perish from priests and counsel from elders, leaving no true guidance
questions.explanation: Verse 26 indicates increasing chaos with loss of true law and counsel, causing people to seek but not find reliable prophetic vision.

hard.title: Ezekiel Chapter 7 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Ezekiel Chapter 7.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 7:19, why will silver and gold not deliver the people in the day of the wrath of the LORD?
options: Because they are cursed by God
Because they are the stumblingblock of their iniquity
Because they were stolen from the temple
Because they were buried underground
questions.correctAnswer: Because they are the stumblingblock of their iniquity
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 7:19 states that silver and gold shall not deliver them because it is the stumblingblock of their iniquity, emphasizing that their wealth is tied to their sin.

questions.question: What did the people make within the beauty of their ornament, according to Ezekiel 7:20?
options: Images of their abominations and detestable things
Altars for foreign gods
Statues of their kings
Tables for offerings to the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: Images of their abominations and detestable things
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 7:20 explains that despite the majesty of their ornament, they made images of their abominations and detestable things, which led God to set it far from them.

questions.question: Who will possess the houses and spoil the land as described in Ezekiel 7:21?
options: The priests and elders
The strangers and the wicked of the earth
The people of Israel
The sons of the prophets
questions.correctAnswer: The strangers and the wicked of the earth
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 7:21 states that God will give the land into the hands of strangers and the wicked of the earth for prey and spoil, showing the judgment on Israel.

questions.question: What consequence is mentioned in Ezekiel 7:22 for God's turning His face from the people?
options: The city will be rebuilt
They shall pollute His secret place as robbers enter and defile it
They will receive a new covenant
The people will prosper in exile
questions.correctAnswer: They shall pollute His secret place as robbers enter and defile it
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 7:22 explains that when God turns His face from them, they shall pollute His secret place because robbers will enter and defile it.

questions.question: What imagery is used in Ezekiel 7:23 to describe the land and city?
options: A land flowing with milk and honey
A land full of bloody crimes and a city full of violence
A land of peace and a city of justice
A land of deserts and a city of refuge
questions.correctAnswer: A land full of bloody crimes and a city full of violence
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 7:23 uses the imagery of making a chain because the land is full of bloody crimes and the city full of violence, symbolizing captivity due to sin.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 7:24, who will God bring to possess the houses and defile the holy places?
options: The priests and Levites
The worst of the heathen
The sons of Israel returning from exile
The remnant of Judah
questions.correctAnswer: The worst of the heathen
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 7:24 says God will bring the worst of the heathen to possess the houses and defile the holy places, indicating judgment through foreign nations.

questions.question: What is the response of the people when destruction comes, as described in Ezekiel 7:25?
options: They will find peace through repentance
They will seek peace, but there shall be none
They will flee to the mountains
They will receive comfort from the prophets
questions.correctAnswer: They will seek peace, but there shall be none
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 7:25 declares that destruction comes and although the people seek peace, none will be found, highlighting the severity of their judgment.

questions.question: Ezekiel 7:26 says 'Mischief shall come upon mischief, and rumour upon rumour.' What will happen to the law and counsel at this time?
options: The law shall be enforced strictly by priests and elders
The law shall perish from the priest, and counsel from the ancients
The law shall be rewritten by the king
The counsel of the ancients shall increase in wisdom
questions.correctAnswer: The law shall perish from the priest, and counsel from the ancients
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 7:26 reveals that during escalating mischief and rumors, the law and counsel will fail as the priests and elders lose their authority.

questions.question: What is the fate of the king and prince as described in Ezekiel 7:27?
options: The king shall reign with peace, and the prince shall be honored
The king shall mourn, and the prince shall be clothed with desolation
The king and prince shall flee to a foreign land
The king shall be exalted, and the prince shall lead the people
questions.correctAnswer: The king shall mourn, and the prince shall be clothed with desolation
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 7:27 states that the king will mourn and the prince will be clothed with desolation, indicating the collapse of leadership as judgment comes.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage similarly warns of the day of the LORD's wrath and judgment as Ezekiel 7?
options: Joel 2:1-2
Genesis 1:1-5
Psalm 23
Proverbs 3:5-6
questions.correctAnswer: Joel 2:1-2
questions.explanation: Joel 2:1-2 also warns of the day of the LORD as a day of darkness, wrath, and destruction, echoing the themes of judgment found in Ezekiel 7:5-7.

questions.question: The Hebrew word translated as 'abominations' in Ezekiel 7:3 and 7:20 primarily refers to what kind of acts?
options: Acts of idolatry and ritual impurity
Acts of charity and kindness
Acts of worship to the LORD
Acts of agriculture and harvest
questions.correctAnswer: Acts of idolatry and ritual impurity
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'to'ebah' translated as 'abominations' refers to detestable acts like idolatry and ritual impurity, as seen in Ezekiel 7:3 and 7:20 where such acts provoke God's judgment.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage reflects the theme of God’s judgment against sin as Ezekiel 7 emphasizes?
options: Revelation 6:12-17
Matthew 5:1-12
Romans 8:28
questions.correctAnswer: Revelation 6:12-17
questions.explanation: Revelation 6:12-17 depicts the day of wrath and judgment similar to Ezekiel 7's warning of the LORD’s anger and the coming destruction upon the sinful.

questions.question: What literary device is prominently used in Ezekiel 7:6-7 where the phrase 'An end is come' is repeated?
options: Chiasm
Parallelism
Repetition for emphasis
Metaphor
questions.correctAnswer: Repetition for emphasis
questions.explanation: The repetition of 'An end is come' in Ezekiel 7:6-7 is a literary device used to emphasize the certainty and imminence of judgment.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 7:19 teaches that wealth in silver and gold can protect the people from the wrath of the LORD.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 7:19 explicitly states that silver and gold shall not be able to deliver them in the day of the LORD's wrath, meaning wealth cannot protect them.

questions.question: True or False: According to Ezekiel 7:27, God's judgment will cause the king and prince to mourn and be clothed with desolation.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 7:27 says the king shall mourn and the prince shall be clothed with desolation as part of God's just judgment upon the land's leaders.

theological.title: Ezekiel Chapter 7 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Ezekiel Chapter 7 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 7:3 reveal about God's response to Israel's abominations?
options: God will send His anger and judge according to their ways
God will forgive and forget their sins
God will bless them with prosperity
God will remain indifferent to their actions
questions.correctAnswer: God will send His anger and judge according to their ways
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 7:3 states that God will send His anger upon Israel and judge them according to their ways, recompensing them for their abominations.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is most clearly demonstrated in Ezekiel 7:4 where God says, 'mine eye shall not spare thee, neither will I have pity'?
options: God's justice and righteousness
God's mercy and grace
God's omniscience
God's omnipresence
questions.correctAnswer: God's justice and righteousness
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 7:4 shows God's justice and righteousness by emphasizing that He will not spare or have pity but will recompense according to their ways.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 7:7 describe the timing and nature of the coming judgment upon the land?
options: The day of trouble is near and cannot be avoided
A time of peace and restoration is coming
The mountains will echo the sound of joy
There will be a delay before judgment
questions.correctAnswer: The day of trouble is near and cannot be avoided
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 7:7 declares that the day of trouble is near for those dwelling in the land and no longer can the mountains sound again as a warning, signifying inevitability.

questions.question: What doctrinal truth about divine retribution is taught in the combination of Ezekiel 7:8 and Ezekiel 7:9?
options: God will judge and recompense according to one's own sinful ways without pity
God will overlook the sins of many for the sake of mercy
God's punishment is delayed indefinitely
God only punishes the innocent
questions.correctAnswer: God will judge and recompense according to one's own sinful ways without pity
questions.explanation: Both verses emphasize that God's fury and anger will be poured out and that He will recompense according to their ways and abominations without sparing or pitying them, affirming the doctrine of perfect divine justice.

questions.question: Ezekiel 7:10 states 'the rod hath blossomed, pride hath budded.' What does this imagery signify in the context of God's judgment?
options: The rise of violence and impending punishment
The beginning of a peaceful reign
The flourishing of righteousness
The establishment of a new covenant
questions.correctAnswer: The rise of violence and impending punishment
questions.explanation: The 'rod' symbolizes a tool of discipline or punishment that has 'blossomed' with pride, indicating the manifestation of violence and evil that leads to God's judgment as seen in verse 10.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 7:11 teach about the fate of those who have risen in violence and wickedness?
options: None of them will remain, nor will there be wailing for them
They will be exalted and celebrated
They will repent and be forgiven
They will escape judgment through sacrifice
questions.correctAnswer: None of them will remain, nor will there be wailing for them
questions.explanation: Verse 11 clearly states that those who have risen in violence and wickedness will be completely removed, and no lamentation will be made for them, underscoring the certainty of judgment.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 7:15, what are the two types of calamities described, and how do they relate to different groups within the land?
options: Sword outside for those in the field; famine and pestilence within the city
Flood and drought for all inhabitants
Peace and prosperity for the righteous
Exile and captivity for the leaders only
questions.correctAnswer: Sword outside for those in the field; famine and pestilence within the city
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 7:15 contrasts the external threat of the sword for those in the field with the internal devastation of famine and pestilence for those in the city, showing the comprehensive nature of judgment.

questions.question: What theological insight about human helplessness in judgment is conveyed by Ezekiel 7:17?
options: All hands shall be feeble and knees weak as water
Humans can overcome judgment through strength
Faith alone guarantees escape from punishment
God will empower the faithful to resist
questions.correctAnswer: All hands shall be feeble and knees weak as water
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 7:17 highlights human helplessness by describing physical weakness and inability to stand in the face of God's coming judgment.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 7:19 illustrate the futility of wealth in the day of the LORD's wrath?
options: Silver and gold cannot deliver or satisfy because they are stumblingblocks of iniquity
Wealth will protect and provide deliverance
Only gold can save from wrath
Wealth ensures eternal life
questions.correctAnswer: Silver and gold cannot deliver or satisfy because they are stumblingblocks of iniquity
questions.explanation: Verse 19 teaches that riches represented by silver and gold are powerless to deliver in judgment and instead are stumblingblocks due to the sinful ways associated with them.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 7:21 prophesy about the fate of Israel's treasures and holy places?
options: They will be given to strangers and wicked people who will profane them
They will be protected and preserved forever
They will be hidden and preserved by faithful priests
They will be returned after a short exile
questions.correctAnswer: They will be given to strangers and wicked people who will profane them
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 7:21 foretells that Israel's treasures will be preyed upon by foreigners and the wicked, leading to pollution and defilement of sacred things.

questions.question: By synthesizing Ezekiel 7:23 and 7:24, what do these verses reveal about the moral condition of the land and God's planned response?
options: The land is full of bloody crimes and violence, so God will bring the worst heathen to possess it and defile holy places
The land is righteous and will be blessed with peace
The land's crimes will be hidden and forgiven without consequence
God will bless the heathen and remove Israel's enemies
questions.correctAnswer: The land is full of bloody crimes and violence, so God will bring the worst heathen to possess it and defile holy places
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 7:23 and 7:24 together depict the deep moral corruption of the land and God's judgment by sending heathen nations to take possession and defile its sacred sites.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal teaching about the inevitability of God's judgment can be drawn from Ezekiel 7:5-6 and Ezekiel 7:25?
options: Evil is certain and destruction is coming with no peace to be found
God's judgment can be delayed indefinitely by repentance
Only the righteous will face destruction
Judgment will be mild and merciful
questions.correctAnswer: Evil is certain and destruction is coming with no peace to be found
questions.explanation: Verses 5-6 declare that an evil, the end, is come, and verse 25 confirms destruction is coming and peace will be sought but not found, showing the certainty and severity of divine judgment.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 7:26-27, what spiritual leadership failure contributes to the downfall of the people, and what is the resulting consequence?
options: The law perishes from the priest and counsel from the ancients, leading to mourning and desolation
The prophets lead the people to victory and peace
The priests teach righteousness and the people prosper
The elders unite to bring spiritual revival
questions.correctAnswer: The law perishes from the priest and counsel from the ancients, leading to mourning and desolation
questions.explanation: Verses 26-27 describe a breakdown in spiritual leadership where law and counsel fail, resulting in mourning by the king and desolation among the people, highlighting the consequences of corrupt leadership.

questions.question: What theological synthesis about God's sovereignty and judgment is revealed by combining Ezekiel 7:2 and Ezekiel 7:27?
options: God sovereignly brings the end upon the land and judges according to their deserts so that they know He is the LORD
God is powerless to stop the destruction
Human efforts alone can save the land from judgment
God's judgment is arbitrary and unjust
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly brings the end upon the land and judges according to their deserts so that they know He is the LORD
questions.explanation: Verse 2 announces the end upon all the land, and verse 27 affirms that God judges according to their ways so that His identity as LORD is known, demonstrating divine sovereignty and just judgment.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that divine judgment in Ezekiel 7 appears excessively harsh and unjust. What does Ezekiel 7:3-4 and 7:9 actually teach about God's judgment?
options: God judges justly and recompenses according to Israel's own sinful ways and abominations, showing righteous justice
God punishes randomly without cause
God's judgment is based on human popularity
God excuses sinners without punishment
questions.correctAnswer: God judges justly and recompenses according to Israel's own sinful ways and abominations, showing righteous justice
questions.explanation: These verses emphasize that God's judgment is a direct response to Israel's sinful ways and abominations, without pity or sparing, underscoring His perfect justice rather than arbitrary cruelty.
